message.content: Lions (family Felidae, order Carnivora) and zebras (family Equidae, order Perissodactyla) do not share a recent common ancestor; they diverged early in the evolution of placental mammals. Their most recent common ancestor is a small, probably insect‑eating mammal that lived roughly 70–80 million years ago, belonging to the clade **Laurasiatheria**. This ancestor was the last common ancestor of the two lineages that later gave rise to the orders Carnivora (which includes lions) and Perissodactyla (which includes zebras).

The last common ancestor would be a mammal from the clade that gave rise to both orders. That would be a member of the clade that includes Perissodactyla and Artiodactyla?
